searchText: Would be nice if there was like a news api that every eth wallet connected to. you mean like an RSS feed? Yes Hey <@636289909359116290> - this project is a step in that direction https://epns.io/ Subscribe to what notifications you want What do you think? I think for widespread use and popularity it needs to be integrated into apps like MetaMask 😛 People that use apps like this probably already regularly check the news. not sure which channel to ask so asking here - given high gas fee in mainnet, why do we still have blocks with 0 transactions? e.g. here https://etherscan.io/block/14007739 This is due to the base fee mechanism introduced in EIP-1599. The gas target is 15M gas per block. Before EIP-1599, in times of high demand the blocks would just simply float around that 15M gas target. After EIP-1599, there are 0M gas (=0 transactions) blocks, but also 30M gas (2x the gas target) blocks, which gives us an average of 15M gas per block. thanks! i'm still not 100% clear why EIP-1559 can't do the same (floating around 15M gas target) I thought the gas cost of a transaction itself is not dependent on the gas price (gwei) which is the major change of EIP-1559.. but I'll read more on it That's up to the miners, has no relation to the eip 1559 It is up to miners to put transactions in a block, the gas target has nothing to do with it Its a bug with geth, though some argue its better to forward an empty block than risk an uncle in some situations. You'll see it happening more to the worse pools like this one https://etherscan.io/blocks?m=0x52bc44d5378309ee2abf1539bf71de1b7d7be3b5&p=2 Just like binance on matic is well known for having empty blocks. wouldn't miners get more rewards and MEVs if they include more transactions? What's the motivation for miners to do this? btw i'm not questioning/blaming eth (or matic/bnb or whatever), just trying to learn. could you expand a bit on why it's a bug with geth? I thought EIP 1559 had something to do with this after I read through <@!273808422753796097> 's doc more. Every bit of gas in your block means that it takes longer to process and propagate, increasing the chance that it will be an uncle This added risk is fairly low, but it is there It's why miners don't accept txs with < 1 gwei priority fee None, miners on those pools are losing out. But it’s like people that go to a store that costs more for the same thing…just not logical and usually due to being lazy or ignorant. Its generally not a big difference too. This isn’t really true. It takes time to process transactions and add them to your candidate block. So you build an empty block and start looking for the PoW solution for it while you process transactions and fill the block. If you happen to find a solution for your empty block before transactions are processed you publish it and pick up and extra block reward that you would have otherwise missed out on if you’d waited to start mining until you had a full block. There is a very low level of this. For the most part though, a lot of pools are just doing things wrong. There are some pools maintaining a ~2-4% rate of empty blocks even before 1559. But your statement was that there was no reason to produce empty blocks which is definitely incorrect and makes the claim that any pool producing them is managed poorly and their miners are lazy and ignorant which is an unreasonable claim to make. Ah, my first statement said "Its a bug with geth, though some argue its better to forward an empty block than risk an uncle in some situations. You'll see it happening more to the worse pools like this one https://etherscan.io/blocks?m=0x52bc44d5378309ee2abf1539bf71de1b7d7be3b5&p=2" Which acknowledged that there is an argument for forwarding empty blocks in some situations. Given that a large percentage of miners mine to pools that pay 5% or more less than they should I think its reasonable to state that many miners are ignorant/lazy. F2Pool is the 2nd biggest despite having hidden fees and stating publicly that its miners are greedy + overpaid. There have been empty blocks both before and after EIP 1559. Empty blocks are rare. I'm not clear on the exact mechanism, but in any case miners want to have all of their mining hardware searching for blocks at all times. Most of the time a given mining rig has a valid tx root, but if not it defaults to an empty root and keeps searching for blocks.

excerpts.author: yblue19

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: This is due to the base fee mechanism introduced in EIP-1599. The gas target is 15M gas per block. Before EIP-1599, in times of high demand the blocks would just simply float around that 15M gas target. After EIP-1599, there are 0M gas (=0 transactions) blocks, but also 30M gas (2x the gas target) blocks, which gives us an average of 15M gas per block.
